problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14225095/assets/a0b4ad67ea80f6d6eec3a15b3df18d551d84263c7424405588bd15162ef4e7c2.png)

The polar curve shown above is defined as

$$
r(\theta) = 4 - 3\cos \theta, \qquad 0\leq \theta < 2\pi.
$$

We have $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ at the point $P.$ The tangent to the curve at $P$ is shown in the diagram. 

To find the equation of the tangent line to the curve at $P,$ we follow four steps.

**Step 1**: Calculate the derivative $\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}.$

Using techniques that we've previously discussed, we can show that

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\theta )=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -3\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta ,\,{x}^{′}(\theta )=3\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta -4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can find $\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )} \\  & =\frac{4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -3\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta }{3\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta -4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Find the slope of the tangent at $P.$

The slope of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})}{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})} \\  & =\frac{4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )}{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})} \\  & =\frac{0+3}{0-4} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P.$

We compute the $xy$-coordinates of $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =(4-3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =(4-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}))\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =0 \\ {y}_{1} & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =(4-3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =(4-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}))\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $\left( 0, 4 \right).$

**Step 4**: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the tangent.

We find the equation of the tangent as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-4 & =-\frac{3}{4}\cdot (x-0) \\ y & =-\frac{3}{4}x+4\end{aligned}
$$
